cases.title: Funnel Intelligence Lab
lines: One campaign cost 4.04× more per approved conversion.
The bridge traced 98.1% of the gap to what happens after
the click: 92.6% of clicks never became an enquiry.
Metric definitions and limits are documented, and CAC is
deliberately not claimed.

cases.title: Appwrite Migration Guard
lines: A read-only Go CLI that snapshots two Appwrite projects and
answers one question: is this migration safe? It returns PASS,
WARN or BLOCK with a reason, never a fake confidence score.
Its docs state the assurance boundary and the known false
negatives. Self-declared pre-alpha.

cases.title: NitroDB
lines: An LSM-tree storage engine in Java: write-ahead log, memtable,
SSTables, bloom filters, MVCC snapshots and leveled compaction,
with concurrency checked by JCStress rather than assumed.

ledger.claim: AetherScan: team of four, six months, quantum on simulator

body: **Problem.** Two campaigns spent $55,662 and $2,893 (19.24× apart) and their cost per approved conversion differed 4.04× ($15.81 vs $63.83).
**Decision it had to support.** Is the gap media cost (CPM), click quality (CTR) or what happens after the click? That decides whether to rework targeting or the landing flow.

**Method.** A sequential-substitution cost bridge: CPM −$3.74, CTR +$4.66, post-click conversion +$47.10, which sums to the $48.02 gap. Click→approved fell from 9.22% to 2.42%, and 92.6% of clicks in the weaker campaign never became an enquiry.

**Limits, stated in the repo.** Observational data from public anonymised ad sets; the campaigns did not run concurrently as an A/B test; attribution order matters; CAC and ROAS are deliberately not computed.
**What comes next.** Five ICE-scored hypotheses sit in the experiment backlog. They are proposals and have not been run.
**Problem.** A backend-as-a-service migration can change a project in ways nobody notices until something breaks.
**Decision.** Return one of three verdicts, PASS, WARN or BLOCK, each with a reason. There is no numeric confidence score, because a score would imply precision the tool does not have.
**Boundary, written down.** `docs/assurance-boundary.md` says what a PASS does and does not mean, and `docs/known-false-negatives.md` lists what the tool can miss.
**Evidence.** 225 passing Go tests, 8 commands, and a fault-injection lab. The README also reports 11 of 11 planted changes caught in a live run; I have not been able to re-run that myself.
**Status.** Self-declared pre-alpha, with no adoption claims.
**Problem.** Public air-quality sources differ in coverage, licence and rate limits, so combining them needs more than concatenation.
**Decision.** Put every source behind one registry that records licence, rate limit and provenance, then build the API on top (53 route handlers).
**My part.** Backend, on a team of four over six months.
**Limits I list myself.** The quantum module runs on a simulator and the repo claims no speed-up. The database is SQLite today, with PostgreSQL planned. The access log is in memory.
**What it is.** An LSM-tree storage engine in Java with a write-ahead log, memtable, SSTables, bloom filters, MVCC snapshots, an off-heap block cache and leveled compaction.
**How I checked it.** 68 unit tests, plus JCStress concurrency tests (3 classes, 42 of 42 outcomes passed in quick mode). JMH benchmark classes exist; I publish no benchmark numbers.

pins: Funnel analytics: traces a 4.04× cost-per-conversion gap to its cause. SQL, Python, live 16-tab dashboard.
Read-only Go CLI that compares two Appwrite projects and returns PASS/WARN/BLOCK with a reason. Documents its own false negatives.
Air-quality analytics platform: FastAPI backend, source registry (licence, rate limit, provenance), Next.js front end. Team of four.
LSM-tree storage engine in Java: WAL, SSTables, MVCC snapshots, leveled compaction. Tested with JUnit and JCStress.
Collaborative document editor on Yjs CRDTs with offline persistence.
